summary.headline: Fiem FY26 revenue rose 16.04% to INR2,790.65 crore and PAT 24.36% to INR253.87 crore, with EBITDA margin at a record 14.09%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 net sales were INR744.35 crore, up 17.44% YoY, with EBITDA of INR109.18 crore (14.67% margin, up from 13.22%) and PAT of INR70.59 crore, up 22.36%. For FY26 the company reported record revenue, PAT and EBITDA margin, and the Board recommended a final dividend of INR40 per share. Management reiterated 15-20% revenue growth for FY27 and a roughly 14% EBITDA margin, and gave the first explicit 4-wheeler revenue range after the CEO's exit. Receivables rose because the company stopped discounting bills with its two major customers, not because of any change in payment terms.

segments.name: Automotive lighting (LED)
segments.commentary: LED share of automotive lighting was 63% in FY26 versus 60% in prior years; management says its pipeline is almost 100% LED and the share will keep rising, with 1-2% gains each quarter.

segments.name: 4-wheeler
segments.commentary: Current 4-wheeler business guided at INR100-150 crore for FY27, rising to INR200-250 crore in FY27-28; Mahindra & Mahindra orders start this year, and Mercedes is at testing and validation stage.

segments.name: Rear-view mirrors and plastic moulded parts
segments.commentary: Share of revenue is slipping slightly, but management says absolute amounts are growing, though more slowly than lighting; these are ancillary products sold to the same lighting customers.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 15-20% a year for FY27 and beyond, ahead of industry growth, despite possible El Nino or weak-monsoon moderation.
EBITDA margin guidance of around 14% or more, including the 4-wheeler business; 4-wheeler expected to be margin-neutral over the next 2-3 years.
4-wheeler revenue: INR100-150 crore in FY27, INR200-250 crore in FY27-28; management says impact is limited this year and more meaningful from next year.
Capex of about INR200 crore over the next two years at company level; no greenfield project envisaged.
Commodity and INR-depreciation cost pressures are treated as pass-through to customers, with a lag of a quarter at times.
Borrowing not needed given healthy cash; insurance premiums to be renegotiated at next renewal.
capex_capacity: Current capacity utilisation about 75%; FY26 capex of about INR108 crore went mainly to debottleneck lines.
Projected capex of about INR200 crore over the next 2 years, which includes the 4-wheeler initiatives.
Solar and open-access renewable energy rollout across plants; Hosur plant gets about 65% of energy from solar and a further 20% from wind, with the model to extend to other plants.
An in-house EMI/EMC validation lab is being installed to cut product development time and reduce reliance on outside test agencies.
R&D spend is more than 2% of revenue (around 2%) in FY26.
demand_pricing: Industry: 2-wheeler production grew about 12% to a record roughly 26.7 million units in FY26, above the FY19 pre-pandemic peak.

Customers: TVS (iQube, Jupiter, Moped, motorcycles), Honda (Activa EV and new models), Royal Enfield (Classic, EV initiatives), Suzuki and Yamaha (healthy growth; 8-9 models in development), Hero (two recent launches running well, and a new EV platform approved).
4-wheeler RFQs of about INR700 crore; about 70% converted into business now under development (management said this does not equal fixed orders).
Pricing: commodity and currency-driven price changes are passed through to customers in both directions.
LED products cost about 3-4x conventional halogen lighting setups, depending on the product.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables jump this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company stopped discounting bills with two major customers, TVS and one other, because cash flow is now strong; payment terms are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other expenses rise faster than revenue, and what is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost was 13.80% of sales in FY26 versus 13.62% earlier, with part of the rise from recently notified labour-cost increases. Capex is about INR200 crore over two years at company level, and no greenfield project is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CEO exit a sign of a delay in the 4-wheeler strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet Sahni left after a three-year term to pursue other interests. Rahul Jain and Rajesh Sharma now lead 4-wheeler, and management says there is no derailment and a detailed strategy will follow.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still looking for a new 4-wheeler CEO?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management says there is enough bandwidth in-house and Rahul Jain, with Rajesh Sharma, will personally oversee 4-wheeler growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will 4-wheeler be margin-accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business is too small to judge separately and will be margin-neutral, with overall EBITDA guidance kept at around 14%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the other automotive lighting (non-LED) growth a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the non-LED share is declining and the chart cited covers the whole company, including rear-view mirrors, not just automotive lighting; it offered to clarify offline.

risks_watch: 4-wheeler execution: order book is still small, Mahindra and Mercedes timelines are not fixed, and the CEO has left.
Demand moderation risk from weak monsoon or El Nino on 2-wheelers.
Cost pass-through lag on commodity and INR-depreciation pressure, including imported LED chips.
Receivables trend after bill discounting was stopped.
Insurance premium increase after the Tapukara fire, to be negotiated at renewal.
Timing of new-product launches (POC stage; regulatory norms for touch and laser technology still awaited).
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins, with firm guidance on 15-20% revenue growth and about 14% EBITDA margin. Cautious and vague on specifics: it declined to name LED penetration targets, product launches and the Hero Splendor question, and gave no date for new technology adoption.
key_quotes: Against this backdrop, Fiem delivered its strongest performance to date.
So for the full year, we continue to maintain our guidance that we will be in the current margin, which is a 14% EBITDA plus is what we target for.
But under no sort of circumstances, should you think that there is any derailment in any way. We are moving forward.
Overall, we can continue to guide even while we grow this business, it will be at neutral margins.
